importance_ranking.reason: Telecom shelter procurement is spec-driven: buyers arrive with defined requirements for shelter type (BTS/Power/Switch Room), size, wall panel type, and IP rating — without matching specs, the listing cannot be evaluated for tender or site deployment. TEC compliance, cooling system, and shelter size are non-interchangeable across project requirements.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant consumer-facing brand with buyer recall exists in Indian telecom shelters — buyers search by TEC approval status, manufacturing capability, and track record with tower companies, not by brand name.
importance_ranking.reason: Institutional buyers (Indus Towers, ATC India, Airtel, Indian Railways) require TEC-approved manufacturers with proven supply track records; an unknown supplier with matching specs is still disqualified without verifiable credentials and certifications.

Visual sub-type variation is meaningful — BTS cabin vs rooftop shelter vs outdoor cabinet vs multi-compartment enclosure are visually distinct, and buyers use images to confirm product type before reading specs. However, image alone cannot close or kill engagement; spec confirmation is the primary gate.

Price varies substantially with shelter size, wall panel type, cooling system, and TEC compliance tier — buyers compare prices only after spec equivalence is confirmed. Final price is always negotiated for institutional orders; listed price serves as a budget entry point and supplier shortlisting signal.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Large custom multi-compartment enclosures (e.g. railway shelters) may be quoted per sq ft, but this is a secondary sub-segment; for the primary BTS shelter segment, per piece is universally implied and never a buyer question.
importance_ranking.reason: Unit is entirely implied for a complete factory-assembled enclosure — no buyer questions whether a telecom shelter is sold per piece.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Defines what the shelter IS and what equipment it houses (BTS vs Power vs Switch Room vs Repeater) — values are non-interchangeable across site deployment requirements and drive the largest price delta in the category.

Footprint (3x3m vs 4x3m vs 6x3m vs custom) directly determines material cost, transport logistics, and site fit — a buyer cannot substitute one size for another, and price scales significantly with floor area.

missing_important_specs.why_important: TEC Generic Requirements (TEC-GR-RS-BSH) compliance is a mandatory procurement signal for licensed telecom operator buyers — absence of this spec prevents institutional buyers from confirming regulatory eligibility.

Foam core density (typically 40 kg/m³) is a primary thermal performance and structural quality differentiator cited by multiple Indian manufacturers and used by buyers to compare insulation quality across suppliers.

PUF panel thickness (50mm, 60mm, 80mm) directly determines thermal insulation performance and compliance with ambient temperature range requirements — a key shortlisting criterion for extreme climate deployments.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Footprint is the primary requirement a seller needs to confirm site fit, material cost, and transport feasibility — without size, no accurate quote is possible.

Panel type (PUF vs EPS vs Rockwool) determines thermal performance tier and compliance with temperature range requirements — sellers need this to confirm product eligibility and price the correct specification.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Sellers need to know whether the buyer requires a BTS cabin, power shelter, switch room, or repeater shelter to confirm they manufacture the correct product type and to price accordingly.
Cooling configuration (DC Aircon, Heat Exchanger, Hybrid, Passive) is a major cost and energy driver — sellers need this to determine equipment fit-out scope and quote accurately.
